data.narrative:
Deep Isolation, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Elizabeth Muller and Richard A. Muller, is evaluated against a comp universe of 11 firms across public and private markets (3 public, 8 private). Same-sector peer set includes Valar Atomics (Series B, $6.0B), Nano Nuclear Energy (Seed, $808M), and Fuse Energy (Series A, $200M).

Two valuation methods are applied. Stage-progression uses the company's $26M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, implying $52M. Peer-median triangulation across three same-sector and same/adjacent-stage companies yields a median of $808M, with range of $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer range reflects stage and capital-intensity variation within early-stage nuclear technology.

The two-method triangulation supports a valuation range of $44M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $430M. The 21x spread between low and high reflects material uncertainty in comparability: the peer median is anchored to one Seed-stage outlier at $808M, while stage-progression suggests more modest valuation relative to capital deployed. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to peers, path to capital efficiency, and whether nuclear sector valuations sustain at observed multiples through market cycles.
